candidate.fit: Material-world travel flavour.

brief.sourceReview: Books IX–XII source pass checked; classification: food-practice-extension. Preserve provisions; inspect supplies; consume them when needed.

candidate.text: On the empty island, abundance waited for people who had not earned it.
candidate.basis: The goat-rich island opposite the Cyclopes is untouched by farming or hunters.
candidate.fit: Natural-world composite.

brief.sourceReview: Books IX–XII source pass checked; classification: natural-world-composite. Find goats on rough ground; hunt; provision the crew.

candidate.text: The goats had the island to themselves until hungry sailors arrived.
candidate.basis: Odysseus's crew hunts the abundant wild goats on the uninhabited island.
candidate.fit: Direct scene with ordinary fauna.

brief.sourceReview: Books IX–XII source pass checked; classification: direct. Find the uninhabited island; hunt its abundant goats; prepare for the cave voyage.

candidate.text: Knowing the monster was coming did not make it a fight he could win.
candidate.basis: Circe warns that Scylla is invincible and instructs Odysseus to pass quickly.
candidate.fit: Foreknowledge without mastery.

brief.sourceReview: Books IX–XII source pass checked; classification: direct. Hear Circe's warning; prepare in advance; stop an approaching threat.
brief.attributes: Foreknowledge does not erase unavoidable loss; it changes how the loss is approached.

candidate.text: His crew obeyed him best by refusing his orders.
candidate.basis: Odysseus orders the crew to bind him tighter if he begs to be released.
candidate.fit: A paradox of trust and restraint.

brief.sourceReview: Books IX–XII source pass checked; classification: direct. Bind Odysseus; secure the mast; free the crew to row.
brief.attributes: Trust means allowing companions to disobey the tempted version of you.

candidate.text: Every gift they mistrusted and every warning they ignored became another verse.
candidate.basis: The wind bag and later cattle episode form a composite cautionary pattern.
candidate.fit: Imagined song explicitly marked as composite.

brief.sourceReview: Books IX–XII source pass checked; classification: imagined-song-composite. Sing of squandered gifts and forbidden food; mourn the lost crew.
brief.attributes: A cautionary performance about the crew's repeated preference for immediate explanation, appetite or wealth.

candidate.text: The cave taught them that escape could be quieter than victory.
candidate.basis: The surviving crew escapes under sheep rather than defeating Polyphemus outright.
candidate.fit: Endurance and stealth over conquest.

brief.sourceReview: Books IX–XII source pass checked; classification: direct. Enter the cave; endure confinement; escape beneath the flock.
brief.attributes: The trial is confinement followed by quiet ingenuity, not a fair fight with the Cyclops.

candidate.text: Every ship entered the passage knowing someone might not leave it.
candidate.basis: Circe says no ship passes Scylla without losing men.
candidate.fit: Setting as unavoidable cost.

brief.sourceReview: Books IX–XII source pass checked; classification: direct-setting. Pass below the cliff; lose companions; continue despite the cost.
brief.attributes: The lair is a place where route choice becomes acceptance of loss.

candidate.text: On Aeaea, welcome and transformation arrived in the same cup.
candidate.basis: Circe's house combines hospitality, food and transforming drugs.
candidate.fit: Place flavour for seductive danger.

brief.sourceReview: Books IX–XII source pass checked; classification: direct-setting. Enter Circe's hall; encounter offered choices; remain on an enchanted island.
brief.attributes: Aeaea makes hospitality and transformation impossible to separate at first glance.

candidate.text: The stone in the doorway mattered more than any weapon inside.
candidate.basis: Polyphemus's immense door-stone makes killing him immediately impossible.
candidate.fit: The cave itself is the prison.

brief.sourceReview: Books IX–XII source pass checked; classification: direct-setting. Endure the cave; hide beneath rams; leave with provisions.
brief.attributes: The cave is the prison because the door-stone removes the obvious violent solution.

candidate.text: Beauty and danger grew from the same enchanted ground.
candidate.basis: Aeaea is Circe's dangerous domain; 'garden' is a treatment, not a named Book XI setting.
candidate.fit: Corrects the old Book XI source drift.

brief.sourceReview: Book X checked: Aeaea is Circe's enchanted domain. The older Book XI label was a source-placement error and is corrected here.
brief.attributes: The garden treatment turns Aeaea's beautiful abundance into visual camouflage for Circe's danger.

candidate.text: She changed bodies before she changed minds.
candidate.basis: Circe's draught and wand transform the crew while the story remains about identity and control.
candidate.fit: Mythic portrayal centred on transformation power.

brief.sourceReview: Books IX–XII source pass checked; classification: direct. Prepare the draught; offer it; turn people into unrecognised creatures.
brief.attributes: The mythic portrayal is Circe at maximum authorship over other bodies and identities.

candidate.text: The sea forgets no crossing; sailors do.
candidate.basis: The whole voyage accumulates remembered routes and losses; the sea-memory premise is an original metaphor.
candidate.fit: Odyssey-wide rather than one episode.

brief.sourceReview: Books IX–XII source pass checked; classification: original-metaphor. Cross again; accumulate routes; draw on remembered passage.
brief.attributes: Experience accumulates even when locations vanish; the voyage leaves mental wakes.

candidate.text: What the sea lost to her returned only when she chose.
candidate.basis: Charybdis cyclically swallows and disgorges the sea.
candidate.fit: Monster identity as recurrence.

brief.sourceReview: Books IX–XII source pass checked; classification: direct. Draw the sea inward; swallow debris; disgorge it again.
brief.attributes: Charybdis is recurrence made monstrous: swallowing and return are parts of the same cycle.

candidate.text: Six mouths made choice irrelevant.
candidate.basis: Scylla strikes simultaneously with six heads and takes six sailors.
candidate.fit: Abrupt predation, not a fair combat.

brief.sourceReview: Books IX–XII source pass checked; classification: direct. Wait above the channel; strike with six heads; take sailors at once.
brief.attributes: Scylla removes the illusion of tactical fairness by attacking six lives at once.

candidate.text: Nothing on Thrinacia escaped the sight of the Sun.
candidate.basis: Helios's sacred cattle are protected by divine awareness and vengeance.
candidate.fit: All-seeing ownership and taboo.

brief.sourceReview: Books IX–XII source pass checked; classification: direct. Keep the cattle sacred; observe the violation; demand retribution.
brief.attributes: Helios is ownership backed by perfect awareness and the power to demand divine enforcement.

candidate.text: He went to the dead because the living had run out of answers.
candidate.basis: Odysseus crosses to the shades specifically to obtain Tiresias's guidance.
candidate.fit: Journey as desperate consultation.

brief.sourceReview: Books IX–XII source pass checked; classification: direct. Reach Ocean's edge; summon shades; hear the dead; leave in fear.
brief.attributes: The descent is a deliberate consultation with fear, grief and obligations the living cannot answer alone.

candidate.text: Hunger made the warning sound negotiable.
candidate.basis: The starving crew knowingly slaughters Helios's cattle despite repeated warnings.
candidate.fit: Temptation becomes collective rationalisation.

brief.sourceReview: Books IX–XII source pass checked; classification: direct. Find sacred cattle; eat despite warning; face destruction.
brief.attributes: The crew knowingly converts sacred property into immediate survival and transfers the cost into the future.

candidate.text: They forgot home before they forgot their own names.
candidate.basis: Lotus-eaters remove the desire to return, not identity by violence.
candidate.fit: Comfort as loss of purpose.

brief.sourceReview: Books IX–XII source pass checked; classification: direct. Taste the lotus; forget departure; be dragged back toward the voyage.
brief.attributes: The Lotus-Eater threat is relief so complete that purpose disappears voluntarily.

candidate.text: The song offered wisdom at the price of ever leaving.
candidate.basis: The Sirens promise knowledge while the bones around them reveal the true cost.
candidate.fit: Knowledge as lethal compulsion.

brief.sourceReview: Books IX–XII source pass checked; classification: direct. Promise knowledge of Troy; draw the listener closer; feed on attention.
brief.attributes: The Sirens weaponise the desire to know more, not simple physical force.

candidate.text: A king among the dead still spoke first of betrayal at home.
candidate.basis: Agamemnon's shade narrates his murder and warns Odysseus about homecoming.
candidate.fit: Bitterness turned into counsel.

brief.sourceReview: Books IX–XII source pass checked; classification: direct. Approach the blood; tell of betrayal at home; warn the living.
brief.attributes: Agamemnon's dead kingship is stripped to warning, resentment and failed homecoming.

candidate.text: Grief gave the dead shape long enough to be remembered.
candidate.basis: The blood-trench scene temporarily gives shades voice and identity; the lament is invented.
candidate.fit: Adaptive lament grounded in ritual.

brief.sourceReview: Books IX–XII source pass checked; classification: imagined-lament. Invite the dead; honour the rite; carry one memory into life.
brief.attributes: An adaptive communal lament gives temporary form to the otherwise scattered voices at the trench.

candidate.text: Punishment became landscape around Tityus.
candidate.basis: Odysseus sees Tityus stretched out under endless avian punishment.
candidate.fit: Visual analogy for the reprint treatment.

brief.sourceReview: Books IX–XII source pass checked; classification: direct-visual. Witness Tityus restrained; see the birds punish him; move on.
brief.attributes: Tityus is punishment as static spectacle: movement is replaced by endless exposure.

candidate.text: The king answered a question by eating the messenger.
candidate.basis: Antiphates kills and eats one scout before the Laestrygonian attack begins.
candidate.fit: Predatory kingship in one action.

brief.sourceReview: Books IX–XII source pass checked; classification: direct. Receive an embassy; seize a man; turn a feast into an attack.
brief.attributes: Antiphates makes kingship indistinguishable from appetite and signals the harbour-wide attack.

candidate.text: They opened the bag for gold and found distance instead.
candidate.basis: The crew mistakes Aeolus's sealed winds for hidden wealth and loses the almost-completed voyage.
candidate.fit: Temptation, force and lost progress.

brief.sourceReview: Books IX–XII source pass checked; classification: direct. Near home; suspect hidden wealth; open the wind bag; lose the route already won.
brief.attributes: The catastrophe begins in envy and suspicion, not ignorance of the bag's physical danger.

candidate.text: Six cries were gone before the oars could change rhythm.
candidate.basis: Scylla takes six sailors at once during the passage.
candidate.fit: Abrupt loss that the crew cannot meaningfully answer.

brief.sourceReview: Books IX–XII source pass checked; classification: direct. Approach the narrow passage; heads strike; six companions disappear.
brief.attributes: The emotional truth is instantaneous subtraction: six companions are simply gone.

candidate.text: Aeolus gave them the wind; envy decided when it would be released.
candidate.basis: Aeolus carefully seals the winds; the crew opens the bag near home.
candidate.fit: Control undone by mistrust.

brief.sourceReview: Books IX–XII source pass checked; classification: direct. Bind hostile winds; store their force; release them unwisely.
brief.attributes: Aeolus's gift is precise control whose safety depends entirely on trust after the giver is absent.

candidate.text: Helios did not need to strike them himself; he only needed Zeus to listen.
candidate.basis: Helios demands punishment after the cattle are killed; Zeus destroys the ship.
candidate.fit: Retribution through divine hierarchy.

brief.sourceReview: Books IX–XII source pass checked; classification: direct. Eat sacred cattle; hear the demand for justice; lose the ship to Zeus's bolt.
brief.attributes: Helios's vengeance is enforcement: sight becomes accusation, accusation becomes Zeus's destruction.

candidate.text: Every headland looked survivable from far enough away.
candidate.basis: Rocky coasts and dangerous approaches recur throughout the wanderings; this land is a composite.
candidate.fit: Landscape danger without false localization.

brief.sourceReview: Books IX–XII source pass checked; classification: landscape-composite. Round a rocky coast under heavy surf.

candidate.text: The dead gave knowledge only to those willing to carry it back.
candidate.basis: The Hades journey is valuable because Odysseus returns with prophecy, obligation and memory.
candidate.fit: Ordeal as listening and return.

brief.sourceReview: Books IX–XII source pass checked; classification: direct-ordeal-adaptation. Approach the dead; hear the owed duty; return with memory.
brief.attributes: The ordeal is listening to the dead and returning alive with obligations still attached.

candidate.text: The narrow sea offered no safe choice, only a survivable one.
candidate.basis: Circe explicitly frames the passage as a choice between dangers, with Scylla the lesser loss.
candidate.fit: Acceptance of necessary danger.

brief.sourceReview: Books IX–XII source pass checked; classification: direct-ordeal-adaptation. Accept the lesser danger; keep rowing; reach water beyond the monsters.
brief.attributes: Success means choosing the loss that still leaves a voyage afterwards.

candidate.text: A crew becomes one body only after every hand accepts the rhythm.
candidate.basis: Coordinated rowing repeatedly determines whether the ship clears danger.
candidate.fit: Rare crew-composite payoff.

brief.sourceReview: Books IX–XII source pass checked; classification: crew-composite. Take the benches; coordinate effort; welcome another hand aboard.
brief.attributes: A crew becomes heroic only as a coordinated body; no single rower is the story.

candidate.text: The shore beyond sight was already shaping the voyage before anyone could name it.
candidate.basis: Unknown shores structure the whole wandering sequence; the Manifest Fate engine is an original exploration metaphor.
candidate.fit: Odyssey-wide GU interpretation.

brief.sourceReview: Books IX–XII source pass checked; classification: exploration-metaphor. Leave a possible route behind; land somewhere unknown; make it productive.
brief.attributes: Unrevealed possibility itself becomes a resource for the next landfall.

flavour.rationale: Basic Land — Mountain. Reserve the basic-land treatment without flavour text.
